reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-3 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: What day of the week comes right after Friday?
What day of the week comes right after Saturday?
What month of the year comes right before December?
What day of the week comes right before Thursday?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: This is a substantial fix from the stale review's calendar-chart date lookups: every sample now tests pure sequencing knowledge ('what comes right after/before X'), matching 'give the days of the week and months of the year in the correct order' with no external chart needed.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only 1 of the 7 samples (seed 44, 'the month right before December') covers months of the year; the other 6 all test days of the week, so the two named domains in this lc are unevenly represented in this batch.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'What day of the week comes right after Friday?' is a single 8-word question, appropriately simple for grade-1 quarter-4 sequencing recall.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: I checked all 7 answers against the standard week/month order (Friday->Saturday, Saturday->Sunday, before December is November, Tuesday->Wednesday, before Thursday is Wednesday, Thursday->Friday) and every one is correct, with both forward ('comes after') and backward ('comes before') phrasing present.

competency_alignment.rationale: The task is now cleanly about sequence recall rather than the calendar-chart date-lookup skill that belongs to a different, harder lc, correctly matching this node's stated scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Testing adjacency (day right before/after) rather than multi-step counting is an appropriate first-exposure difficulty for grade-1 quarter-4 sequencing.
